deduped_items.title: Central Bank of Egypt says US measures against Banque Misr UAE branch will not impact domestic sector
deduped_items.summary: The Central Bank of Egypt confirmed that recent United States measures imposed on Banque Misr’s branch in the United Arab Emirates, in connection with economic restrictions on Iran, will not impact the Egyptian banking sector or the bank’s domestic operations. US Dollar Transactions Restricted The central bank stressed that the US action is strictly limited […] The post Central Bank of Egypt says US measures against Banque Misr UAE branch will not impact domestic sector first appeared on Dailyne
deduped_items.body_text:
The Central Bank of Egypt confirmed that recent United States measures imposed on Banque Misr’s branch in the United Arab Emirates, in connection with economic restrictions on Iran, will not impact the Egyptian banking sector or the bank’s domestic operations.
US Dollar Transactions Restricted
The central bank stressed that the US action is strictly limited to the UAE branch’s transactions with correspondent banks in US dollars.
The measures do not extend to any other institutions within the Egyptian banking sector, including Banque Misr in Egypt or any of its other foreign branches, with the scope explicitly confined to the dollar transactions of the UAE branch.
Central Bank of Egypt Highlights Sector Resilience and Diplomatic Efforts
The central bank and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs are currently in contact with US authorities to monitor the measures and address their repercussions, the statement noted.
In a final message directed at reassuring depositors, the Central Bank of Egypt affirmed the strength and resilience of all banks operating in Egypt. The regulator emphasised the soundness and solidity of the Egyptian banking sector in the face of external developments.

deduped_items.title: Al-Sisi orders review of real estate contracts and electricity bills in sweeping domestic directives
deduped_items.summary: President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi has issued a raft of domestic directives aimed at improving living conditions. He ordered immediate actions on real estate accountability, electricity billing, market controls, and traffic discipline during a speech on Monday. Speaking at the Strategic Command headquarters in the New Administrative Capital during a ceremony marking the Prophet Muhammad’s birthday, […] The post Al-Sisi orders review of real estate contracts and electricity bills in sweeping domestic
deduped_items.body_text:
President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi has issued a raft of domestic directives aimed at improving living conditions. He ordered immediate actions on real estate accountability, electricity billing, market controls, and traffic discipline during a speech on Monday.
Speaking at the Strategic Command headquarters in the New Administrative Capital during a ceremony marking the Prophet Muhammad’s birthday, Al-Sisi assured the public of the state’s vigilance regarding national security, affirming that the armed forces are fully prepared to defend the country against external threats. He stressed that his focus extends beyond military readiness to addressing accumulated domestic challenges and improving citizen services.
To increase transparency, the president ordered the government to prepare a comprehensive report detailing actual achievements, expenditures, and results across all state sectors over the past years. This report will be presented to the public during a conference scheduled for October, which will include intellectuals, specialists, and university professors to discuss implemented projects and ongoing challenges over a period of a week to ten days.
Al-Sisi delivered a stern warning regarding the real estate sector, mandating close monitoring of contracts to ensure developers do not delay the delivery of units or the construction of associated infrastructure. He announced a comprehensive review by state agencies to ensure developers fulfil their obligations. “I will be sharp on this matter,” Al-Sisi said. “Anyone who takes money from people is obligated to execute the contract on time, and legal measures will be taken to protect citizens’ rights.”
Addressing utility costs, the president directed the Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy to directly supervise billing to prevent arbitrary estimations. He ordered the implementation of measures to facilitate the payment of overdue balances.
On food security, Al-Sisi instructed the Minister of Supply and Internal Trade to continuously control markets and expand government sales outlets, mandating the establishment of at least one government outlet in every district nationwide to provide basic commodities at prices matching citizens’ purchasing power.
Responding to a recent rise in traffic accidents, the president ordered the Minister of Interior to launch continuous traffic campaigns to enforce strict discipline and rapidly process violations. He also directed the Minister of Transport to complete all mass transit projects within their set timeframes and continuously improve road conditions.
Furthermore, Al-Sisi reiterated instructions to the Ministry of Local Development and provincial governors to conduct on-the-ground monitoring, open direct communication channels with citizens, address complaints, and ensure strict accountability for violators.
He concluded by stressing that the rule of law must be enforced decisively, stating that there is “no place among us for the corrupt, nor any favouritism for those who manipulate the people’s rights or tamper with the destiny of this great nation.”

US Dollar Transactions Restricted The central bank stressed that the US action is strictly limited […] The post Central Bank of Egypt says US measures against Banque Misr UAE branch will not impact domestic sector first appeared on Dailyne
deduped_items.body_text:
The Central Bank of Egypt confirmed that recent United States measures imposed on Banque Misr’s branch in the United Arab Emirates, in connection with economic restrictions on Iran, will not impact the Egyptian banking sector or the bank’s domestic operations.
US Dollar Transactions Restricted
The central bank stressed that the US action is strictly limited to the UAE branch’s transactions with correspondent banks in US dollars.
The measures do not extend to any other institutions within the Egyptian banking sector, including Banque Misr in Egypt or any of its other foreign branches, with the scope explicitly confined to the dollar transactions of the UAE branch.
Central Bank of Egypt Highlights Sector Resilience and Diplomatic Efforts
The central bank and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs are currently in contact with US authorities to monitor the measures and address their repercussions, the statement noted.
In a final message directed at reassuring depositors, the Central Bank of Egypt affirmed the strength and resilience of all banks operating in Egypt. The regulator emphasised the soundness and solidity of the Egyptian banking sector in the face of external developments.

deduped_items.title: USF strikes another 21 energy facilities in temporarily occupied territories and Luhansk TPP
deduped_items.summary: The Unmanned Systems Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, as part of the "Crimean Switch Off" operation, struck another 21 energy facilities in the temporarily occupied territories of Donetsk, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia regions, as well as in Crimea, and the Luhansk Thermal Power Plant over three days from August 26 to 28.

deduped_items.title: ISU изменил правила допуска фигуристов на Гран-при
deduped_items.body_text:
Международный союз конькобежцев (ISU) изменил правила допуска российских и белорусских фигуристов на турниры серии Гран-при. Об этом сообщается на сайте «Спорт-Экспресс».
Для попадания в список запасных на этапы Гран-при спортсменам необходимо участвовать в турнирах серии «Челленджер» и набирать установленный минимум баллов. Победители этих турниров будут добавлены в нижнюю часть списка запасных, где сформируется мини-рейтинг в соответствии с набранными баллами.
Также ISU отменил бонус для призеров Гран-при, который ранее давал приоритетное право на участие во втором этапе серии. Слово «медаль» в новом документе не встречается ни разу.
Как приводит Sports.ru слова журналиста Майи Багрянцевой, изменения существенно затрудняют оперативное получение второго этапа нейтральным спортсменам. «Победа на "Челленджере" больше не означает попадание в список запасных на общих условиях», — отметила она.
Ранее 30 июня 2026 года ISU допустил российских и белорусских спортсменов до международных соревнований в сезоне-2026/27 в нейтральном статусе. Среди затронутых новыми правилами — Аделия Петросян и Петр Гуменник, выступавшие на Олимпийских играх-2026.

deduped_items.title: В России прокомментировали видео с «закрытого совещания» по мобилизации
deduped_items.body_text:
Распространяемое в социальных сетях видео с «закрытого совещания» властей Мурманской области по мобилизации является фейком. Об этом сообщил региональный оперштаб в своем Telegram-канале.
Ведомство прокомментировало видео, на котором губернатор области Андрей Чибис в ходе совещания рассказывает о предстоящей мобилизации в регионе.
«В интернет вбросили очередное фейковое видео якобы с участием губернатора Чибиса. Будьте бдительны — сегодня с помощью нейросетей возможно создать видео с лицом и голосом любого человека. Пожалуйста, пользуйтесь только проверенными источниками информации», — указано в сообщении.
Ранее официальный представитель МИД РФ Мария Захарова назвала источник слухов о мобилизации в России. По ее словам, «инспирированные украинской хунтой и ее западными покровителями спекуляции о якобы возможной в нашей стране мобилизации» неоднократно опровергались российскими официальными лицами.

deduped_items.title: В Грузии задержали иностранца за убийство россиянина
deduped_items.body_text:
Силовики задержали гражданина иностранного государства, который расправился, предположительно, над российским туристом в Тбилиси. Об этом сообщили в МВД республики, передает РИА Новости.
Уточняется, что задержание провели сотрудники Тбилисского управления полиции МВД. Иностранца задержали по горячим следам. Ему вменяют умышленное убийство.
Как удалось установить предварительно, в столице Грузии между двумя иностранными гражданами разгорелся конфликт. В ходе него один из участников перепалки нанес второму ранения с использованием холодного оружия, а также тупого предмета. Нападавший скрылся.
По информации ведомства, расследование идет по статье 108 Уголовного кодекса Грузии. Она предполагает наказание в виде лишения свободы на срок до 15 лет.
Ранее телеканал «ТВ Пирвели» сообщил, что 40-летний россиянин был убит после конфликта в супермаркете. Инцидент произошел на подъеме Бараташвили.

deduped_items.title: В Херсонской области после атаки БПЛА пропал свет
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- В Херсонской области отсутствует электроснабжение после атаки БПЛА.
- Аварийные бригады приступили к восстановительным работам на поврежденном оборудовании подстанций.
МОСКВА, 28 авг - РИА Новости. Электроснабжение отсутствует в Херсонской области после атаки БПЛА, повреждено оборудование, аварийные бригады приступили к восстановительным работам, сообщил губернатор региона Владимир Сальдо. 
"По информации министерства топливно-энергетического комплекса Херсонской области, с прошлой ночи в регионе отсутствует электроснабжение. Причина - очередная атака противника на энергетическую инфраструктуру. К сожалению, несколько украинских беспилотников достигли подстанций и повредили оборудование", - написал Сальдо в канале на платформе "Макс". 
Он отметил, что аварийные бригады уже работают над восстановлением электроснабжения. По словам губернатора, заранее назвать сроки возвращения света пока невозможно, информация будет предоставлена после подтверждения.

- Крупнейшая украинская сеть супермаркетов «АТБ» ввела ограничения на продажу некоторых категорий товаров в одни руки.
- Ограничения касаются бакалеи, мясных и рыбных консервов, куриных яиц и некоторых других категорий товаров, включая покупки в магазинах и онлайн-заказы.
МОСКВА, 28 авг - РИА Новости. Крупнейшая украинская сеть супермаркетов "АТБ" ввела ограничения на продажу в одни руки некоторых категорий товаров, сообщает издание "Страна.ua". 
"В крупнейшей украинской сети супермаркетов "АТБ" ... введены ограничения на продажу товаров в одни руки", - говорится в сообщении, опубликованном в Telegram-канале издания. 
По данным ресурса, новые правила касаются как покупок в магазинах, так и онлайн-заказов. Согласно данным, ограничения введены на бакалею, мясные и рыбные консервы, куриные яйца и некоторые другие категории товаров.

deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Под Киевом около Житомирской трассы прогремели взрывы.
- На месте взрывов начался сильный пожар, была зафиксирована повторная детонация.
МОСКВА, 28 авг - РИА Новости. Взрывы прогремели под Киевом около Житомирской трассы, на месте начался сильный пожар, сообщает телеканал "Мы - Украина" со ссылкой на столичные сообщества. 
"Под Киевом прогремели взрывы: сообщают о сильном пожаре. Вблизи Житомирской трассы очевидцы сообщают о масштабном пожаре и мощных взрывах", - говорится в сообщении, опубликованном в Telegram-канале СМИ. 
Как сообщает ресурс, на месте, по предварительным данным, была также зафиксирована повторная детонация.

deduped_items.title: Selenskyj entließ ihn – jetzt arbeitet Ex-Minister Fedorow für Italien
deduped_items.summary: Nach seinem erzwungenen Abschied aus der ukrainischen Regierung wechselt Mychajlo Fedorow nach Italien. Als Berater soll er Verteidigungsminister Guido Crosetto bei Militärtechnologie unterstützen – und zugleich weiter an Projekten für die Ukraine arbeiten.
deduped_items.body_text:
Selenskyj entließ ihn – jetzt arbeitet Ex-Minister Fedorow für Italien
Nach seinem erzwungenen Abschied aus der ukrainischen Regierung wechselt Mychajlo Fedorow nach Italien. Als Berater soll er Verteidigungsminister Guido Crosetto bei Militärtechnologie unterstützen – und zugleich weiter an Projekten für die Ukraine arbeiten.
Klicken Sie hier, um sich Artikel von WELT in der Google-Suche bevorzugt anzeigen zu lassen.
Der aus dem Amt gedrängte ukrainische Verteidigungsminister Mychailo Fedorow wird „Berater für Innovationen in der Verteidigung“ des italienischen Verteidigungsministers Guido Crosetto. Dieser habe ihm die Stelle angeboten, erklärte Fedorow am Freitag in Onlinediensten. „In dieser Funktion werde ich Italien dabei unterstützen, Technologien für die moderne Kriegsführung zu entwickeln.“ Gleichzeitig werde er weiter „an Projekten zur Stärkung der Verteidigungsfähigkeit“ der Ukraine arbeiten.
Das italienische Verteidigungsministerium bezeichnete die Ankündigung als „wichtige Chance“ für Italien und teilte mit, Fedorow werde als „Innovationsberater“ fungieren. Dieser verfüge über „umfangreiche Erfahrungen“ mit „autonomen Systemen und mit der Luftverteidigung“.
Lesen Sie auch
Der italienischen Zeitung „La Repubblica“ zufolge hatte Crosetto Fedorow bereits im Juli eine Beraterstelle angeboten. Fedorows Büro zufolge wird er weiter in Kiew bleiben und von dort aus arbeiten. Von der ukrainischen Präsidialverwaltung gab es zunächst keine Stellungnahme.
Der technikaffine 35-jährige Fedorow war vor sechs Wochen vom ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj aus dem Amt gedrängt worden. Grund waren offenbar Spannungen zwischen dem Minister und der Armeeführung. In der Folge gingen tausende Ukrainer auf die Straße und verlangten Fedorows Wiedereinsetzung.
Anfang August forderte Fedorow dann Wahlen in der Ukraine, was das Verhältnis zu Selenskyj weiter eintrübte. Wegen des seit Beginn der russischen Invasion im Februar 2022 geltenden Kriegsrechts sind Wahlen ausgesetzt. Selenskyjs reguläre Amtszeit als Präsident endete im Mai 2024. Er wies den Vorschlag zurück, weil dieser das Land „spaltet“.
Noch immer gehen in Kiew Menschen für Fedorow auf die Straße. Kürzlich sagte der Ex-Minister in einer Videobotschaft, die Ukraine benötige einen „rechtmäßigen, sicheren und realistischen Mechanismus“, um während eines langwierigen Krieges Wahlen abzuhalten. Demokratie sei kein „Friedenszeiten-Luxus“, so Fedorow. Russland dürfe nicht erlaubt werden, die Demokratie als Geisel zu nehmen.

Nach seinem erzwungenen Abschied aus der ukrainischen Regierung wechselt Mychajlo Fedorow nach Italien. Als Berater soll er Verteidigungsminister Guido Crosetto bei Militärtechnologie unterstützen – und zugleich weiter an Projekten für die Ukraine arbeiten.
Klicken Sie hier, um sich Artikel von WELT in der Google-Suche bevorzugt anzeigen zu lassen.
Der aus dem Amt gedrängte ukrainische Verteidigungsminister Mychailo Fedorow wird „Berater für Innovationen in der Verteidigung“ des italienischen Verteidigungsministers Guido Crosetto. Dieser habe ihm die Stelle angeboten, erklärte Fedorow am Freitag in Onlinediensten. „In dieser Funktion werde ich Italien dabei unterstützen, Technologien für die moderne Kriegsführung zu entwickeln.“ Gleichzeitig werde er weiter „an Projekten zur Stärkung der Verteidigungsfähigkeit“ der Ukraine arbeiten.
Das italienische Verteidigungsministerium bezeichnete die Ankündigung als „wichtige Chance“ für Italien und teilte mit, Fedorow werde als „Innovationsberater“ fungieren. Dieser verfüge über „umfangreiche Erfahrungen“ mit „autonomen Systemen und mit der Luftverteidigung“.
Lesen Sie auch
Der italienischen Zeitung „La Repubblica“ zufolge hatte Crosetto Fedorow bereits im Juli eine Beraterstelle angeboten. Fedorows Büro zufolge wird er weiter in Kiew bleiben und von dort aus arbeiten. Von der ukrainischen Präsidialverwaltung gab es zunächst keine Stellungnahme.
Der technikaffine 35-jährige Fedorow war vor sechs Wochen vom ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj aus dem Amt gedrängt worden. Grund waren offenbar Spannungen zwischen dem Minister und der Armeeführung. In der Folge gingen tausende Ukrainer auf die Straße und verlangten Fedorows Wiedereinsetzung.
Anfang August forderte Fedorow dann Wahlen in der Ukraine, was das Verhältnis zu Selenskyj weiter eintrübte. Wegen des seit Beginn der russischen Invasion im Februar 2022 geltenden Kriegsrechts sind Wahlen ausgesetzt. Selenskyjs reguläre Amtszeit als Präsident endete im Mai 2024. Er wies den Vorschlag zurück, weil dieser das Land „spaltet“.
Noch immer gehen in Kiew Menschen für Fedorow auf die Straße. Kürzlich sagte der Ex-Minister in einer Videobotschaft, die Ukraine benötige einen „rechtmäßigen, sicheren und realistischen Mechanismus“, um während eines langwierigen Krieges Wahlen abzuhalten. Demokratie sei kein „Friedenszeiten-Luxus“, so Fedorow. Russland dürfe nicht erlaubt werden, die Demokratie als Geisel zu nehmen.

deduped_items.title: Debatte: Wir wissen doch, was geschah
deduped_items.summary: Über 200 Jahre erkämpfte Deutschland sich ein demokratisches Grundgesetz – dann gab man es her, weil einige glaubten, die Regierung Hitler sei nur ein kurzer Spuk. Was ein Blick bis in die Zeit Goethes uns über die Gegenwart lehrt.
deduped_items.body_text:
Die Berliner U-Bahn-Linie 9 ist besonders laut, Quietschen, Schienenschlagen und metallisches Geklapper. Das Telefon vibrierte, ich verstand nichts, versprach einen Rückruf an der nächsten Station – Spichernstraße. Mike Josef, Oberbürgermeister von Frankfurt: Die Jury habe mir den Goethe-Preis zugesprochen, ob ich den Preis annehme? Ich habe nicht lange nachdenken müssen.
DebatteWir wissen doch, was geschah
Lesezeit: 9 Min.
Über 200 Jahre erkämpfte Deutschland sich ein demokratisches Grundgesetz – dann gab man es her, weil einige glaubten, die Regierung Hitler sei nur ein kurzer Spuk. Was ein Blick bis in die Zeit Goethes uns über die Gegenwart lehrt.
Gastbeitrag von Uwe Timm
Die AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt will dem Land Stolz einflößen – mit weniger Bauhaus und mehr Pflege von Kriegerdenkmälern. Ausgedacht hat sich die Identitätsfolklore Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, ein in Rumänien geborener Islamwissenschaftler.

deduped_items.title: Usa, Colombia ed Ecuador rafforzano coordinamento nella lotta contro i cartelli
deduped_items.summary: "Gettate le basi per una nuova era di operazioni decisive e unificate in tutta la regione"
deduped_items.body_text:
Colombia ed Ecuador con il sostegno
degli Stati Uniti mirano a rafforzare il coordinamento nella
lotta contro i gruppi armati e i cartelli della droga che
operano nella zona di confine tra i due Paesi.
                                    
                                       
				   E' quanto emerso al termine di un incontro avvenuto nella
città ecuadoriana di San Lorenzo, al confine con la Colombia,
tra il comandante in capo del Comando Sud degli Stati Uniti,
Francis L. Donovan, e i ministri della Difesa dell'Ecuador, Gian
Carlo Loffredo, e della Colombia, Jorge Eduardo Mora.
                                    
                                       
				   "Stiamo portando avanti la lotta contro i narcotrafficanti
per porre fine al loro terrore e alla loro violenza
nell'emisfero occidentale e per proteggere la patria. Gli
incontri di questa settimana del Comandante del Comando Sud,
Generale Francis L. Donovan, con i leader militari colombiani ed
ecuadoriani hanno gettato le basi per una nuova era di
operazioni decisive e unificate in tutta la regione", riferisce
oggi un post su X del South Command.
                                    
                                       
				   Il ministero della Difesa dell'Ecuador parla della creazione
di un "tridente della sicurezza" e riferisce che "funzionari
della difesa dei tre Paesi hanno coordinato gli sforzi per
rafforzare la condivisione di informazioni, il coordinamento
operativo e le capacità di risposta contro le organizzazioni
criminali transnazionali che operano lungo il confine
settentrionale".

deduped_items.title: El Sevilla FC negocia con el Leipzig por Conrad Harder

El Sevilla FC negocia con el Leipzig por Conrad Harder
El delantero no tendría sitio tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu por el conjunto alemán
El Sevilla FC ya se ha decidido por un delantero para completar su nóminas de arietes. Se trata de Conrad Harder, el futbolista noruego del Leipzig que acaba de quedarse sin sitio en su equipo tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu ... por el conjunto alemán. Se da la circunstancia de que el delantero catalán también estuvo entre las opciones del Sevilla para su delantera. Sin embargo la operación era económicamente viable, aunque el jugador estaba por la labor de bajarse el sueldo, seguía siendo insuficiente para que el Sevilla pudiera hacerle un hueco en la plantilla.
Ahora, aunque también ha tanteado al serbio Ratkov, a José Ignacio Navarro le gusta más la opción de Harder. Las negociaciones están abiertas dese hace unos días, tal y como ha adelantado El Chiringuito. Según ha podido conocer este medio, el Sevilla se encuentra muy bien posicionado para hacerse con la cesión de este delantero, por el que el Leipzig abonó unos 24 millones de euros. Se confía en que la operación se cierre pronto y, al fin, se cierre el apartado del tercer delantero.
Esta incorporación era una de las exigencias prioritarias de Luis García Plaza. Si bien a José Ignacio Navarro le ha costado dar con un perfil interesante, que encaje con las posibilidades económicas sevillistas. El club tiene unos dos millones de euros de límite, que estaba destinado para el ariete ansiado. Se seguirá liberando con la salida de Vargas y alguna otra más que pueda concretarse de aquí al martes, pero la dirección deportiva ha querido zanjar ya este tema y se confía en que el acuerdo con el Leipzig llegue pronto.
Varias intentonas frustradas
El Sevilla estuvo muy cerca de tener a George Ilenikhena cerrado como cedido, pero los problemas financieros del Al-Ittihad bloquearon la operación. Era el perfil que más convencía a Luis García Plaza, puesto que complementaba a Robbie Ure, por el que el club ha pagado más de seis millones de euros. El Sevilla ha mantenido ciertas esperanzas en torno al posible desbloqueo de la situación del franco-nigeriano, pero el final del mercado acecha y había que mover ficha, más aún tras el rapapolvo de García Plaza hoy en rueda de prensa.
El Sevilla ha tanteado los nombres de Guiu y de Ratkov. El primero, demasiado caro, y el segundo no terminaba de convencer ni al entrenador ni al director deportivo. Hace unos días, el Sevilla preguntó por la situación de Conrad Harder, al que el Leipzig le está buscando una salida en este mercado, bien fuera como cesión o traspaso. Ante la imposibilidad de vender al delantero por un precio cercano a lo que costó, el préstamo es la vía más fácil y José Ignacio Navarro quiere cerrarlo lo antes posible.

El regreso de Abde, la gran novedad de la convocatoria para el segundo partido de la semana del conjunto de Pellegrini en Valencia
Segundo partido de la semana para el Real Betis, que ganó en Mestalla el aplazado de la primera jornada el pasado martes y este sábado regresa a la capital del Turia para medirse al Levante UD. Con la satisfacción del trabajo bien ... hecho y la moral reforzada, gracias a los seis puntos que lustran ya su casillero, llegan los de Pellegrini a esta cita correspondiente a la tercera jornada de LaLiga EA Sports. Frente al pleno verdiblanco, el uno de seis de su rival, que cayó con el Espanyol y empató a domicilio con el Osasuna. De Burgos Bengoetxea, con Pulido Santana en el VAR, arbitrarán este choque en el Ciutat de Valencia.
Con el golazo de Pablo García en un contragolpe bien enjaretado en la recta final del choque, el Betis se llevó todo el botín de Valencia y sumó su segundo triunfo al casillero dejando su portería a cero. Un añadido que siempre abrillanta más el trabajo y produce mayor satisfacción tanto en los jugadores como en el entrenador, el siempre ambicioso Pellegrini en este caso, que cambió a toda la línea defensiva respecto al duelo con la Real en una apuesta que le salió a pedir de boca.
El posible once del Betis ante el Levante
Abde, que se ha ejercitado en los últimos días con el equipo, constituye la principal novedad de la convocatoria del Betis, que se marchó hasta Valencia con estos 23 futbolistas: Valles, Manu González, Álvaro de Pablo, Ángel Ortiz, Bellerín, Natan, Bartra, Llorente, V. Gómez, Fran García, Facundo Bernal, Losada, Deossa, Marc Roca, Fornals, Fidalgo, Isco, Pablo García, Antony, Abde, Riquelme, Parrott, Cucho Hernández. Causan baja Lo Celso, Aitor, Morante, Petit, Diego Conde y Junior.
Real Betis: Valles; Bellerín, Bartra, Natan, Fran García; Marc Roca, Deossa; Antony, Fornals, Riquelme; Parrott.
El posible once del Levante ante el Betis
El Levante UD se estrena este sábado ante su público, en el Ciutat de Valencia, después de un discreto comienzo de temporada. En la primera jornada fue goleado por el Espanyol (3-0) y en la segunda rascó un empate en Pamplona (0-0), pero volvió a quedarse sin marcar. El conjunto granota, que salvó la categoría la pasada campaña con una gran recta final de curso, se afana en buscar un sustituto para Carlos Espí. Para jugar de punta, el técnico Luis Castro cuenta con el joven belga Musuayi, Etta Eyong e Iván Romero, titular en las dos primeras jornadas.
Levante UD: Ryan; Toljan, Dela, Mandi, Manu Sánchez; Oriol Rey, Olasagasti, Bardeli; Brugui, Thiago, Iván Romero.
Mandi, Hugo Sotelo, Enzo Bardeli, Thiago Fernández y el citado Musuayi son los fichajes más importantes que ha acometido el club granota en la presente ventana de mercado, aún abierta. En el capítulo de bajas hay que apuntar la del mediocampista Pablo Martínez. Para este duelo con el Betis, Castro cuenta en principio con todo el plantel disponible a excepción del lesionado Alejandro Primo.

deduped_items.body_text:
El Sevilla FC negocia con el Leipzig por Conrad Harder
El delantero no tendría sitio tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu por el conjunto alemán
El Sevilla FC ya se ha decidido por un delantero para completar su nóminas de arietes. Se trata de Conrad Harder, el futbolista noruego del Leipzig que acaba de quedarse sin sitio en su equipo tras el fichaje de Marc Guiu ... por el conjunto alemán. Se da la circunstancia de que el delantero catalán también estuvo entre las opciones del Sevilla para su delantera. Sin embargo la operación era económicamente viable, aunque el jugador estaba por la labor de bajarse el sueldo, seguía siendo insuficiente para que el Sevilla pudiera hacerle un hueco en la plantilla.
Ahora, aunque también ha tanteado al serbio Ratkov, a José Ignacio Navarro le gusta más la opción de Harder. Las negociaciones están abiertas dese hace unos días, tal y como ha adelantado El Chiringuito. Según ha podido conocer este medio, el Sevilla se encuentra muy bien posicionado para hacerse con la cesión de este delantero, por el que el Leipzig abonó unos 24 millones de euros. Se confía en que la operación se cierre pronto y, al fin, se cierre el apartado del tercer delantero.
Esta incorporación era una de las exigencias prioritarias de Luis García Plaza. Si bien a José Ignacio Navarro le ha costado dar con un perfil interesante, que encaje con las posibilidades económicas sevillistas. El club tiene unos dos millones de euros de límite, que estaba destinado para el ariete ansiado. Se seguirá liberando con la salida de Vargas y alguna otra más que pueda concretarse de aquí al martes, pero la dirección deportiva ha querido zanjar ya este tema y se confía en que el acuerdo con el Leipzig llegue pronto.
Varias intentonas frustradas
El Sevilla estuvo muy cerca de tener a George Ilenikhena cerrado como cedido, pero los problemas financieros del Al-Ittihad bloquearon la operación. Era el perfil que más convencía a Luis García Plaza, puesto que complementaba a Robbie Ure, por el que el club ha pagado más de seis millones de euros. El Sevilla ha mantenido ciertas esperanzas en torno al posible desbloqueo de la situación del franco-nigeriano, pero el final del mercado acecha y había que mover ficha, más aún tras el rapapolvo de García Plaza hoy en rueda de prensa.
El Sevilla ha tanteado los nombres de Guiu y de Ratkov. El primero, demasiado caro, y el segundo no terminaba de convencer ni al entrenador ni al director deportivo. Hace unos días, el Sevilla preguntó por la situación de Conrad Harder, al que el Leipzig le está buscando una salida en este mercado, bien fuera como cesión o traspaso. Ante la imposibilidad de vender al delantero por un precio cercano a lo que costó, el préstamo es la vía más fácil y José Ignacio Navarro quiere cerrarlo lo antes posible.

deduped_items.title: MPs demand broadcaster be taken off of the air after panelists praised Adolf Hitler
deduped_items.summary: A large majority of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of Dutch parliament, is urging culture minister Rianne Letscher to take decisive action, including potentially revoking the broadcasting licens
deduped_items.body_text:
MPs demand broadcaster be taken off of the air after panelists praised Adolf Hitler
A large majority of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of Dutch parliament, is urging culture minister Rianne Letscher to take decisive action, including potentially revoking the broadcasting license of far-right broadcaster Ongehoord Nederland (ON!) after the company praised Hitler in one of its panel shows, RTL Nieuws reports.
Pressure has mounted in the last week after the incident occurred on the online panel show Let’s Twist Again. MPs and critics have accused the segment of normalizing and justifying Nazi ideology by portraying Adolf Hitler as an “anti-globalist crusader.”A public petition demanding the removal of Ongehoord Nederland quickly garnered over 20,000 signatures.
MPs from a wide range of parties, including PRO, D66 and CDA, have condemned the broadcast. They declared that the political patience with the broadcaster has completely run out. Parliament wants ON! permanently removed from the Dutch broadcasting system. The Tweede Kamer has officially scheduled a parliamentary debate on the future of ON! for September 24.
Letschert has said that she is actively exploring all legal options to intervene. She openly discussed the possibility of stripping ON! of its broadcasting license but warned that doing so requires strict, legally airtight criteria.
Letschert emphasized that she cannot simply ban the broadcaster by decree, as a judge would immediately overturn an arbitrary decision. ON! must be proven to have systematically violated the Media Act and journalistic standards.
ON! was also in hot water a few months earlier. In June, ten fellow public broadcasters sent a joint letter to Letschert refusing to cooperate with ON! due to repeated violations of the journalistic code of conduct.
While the overarching NPO organization acknowledged that ON! regularly breaks the Code of Journalistic Conduct, the NPO stated it lacks the legal mandate to issue sanctions or formally request the minister to expel them. This kicked the responsibility back to Letschert and parliament.

MPs and critics have accused the segment of normalizing and justifying Nazi ideology by portraying Adolf Hitler as an “anti-globalist crusader.”A public petition demanding the removal of Ongehoord Nederland quickly garnered over 20,000 signatures.
MPs from a wide range of parties, including PRO, D66 and CDA, have condemned the broadcast. They declared that the political patience with the broadcaster has completely run out. Parliament wants ON! permanently removed from the Dutch broadcasting system. The Tweede Kamer has officially scheduled a parliamentary debate on the future of ON! for September 24.
Letschert has said that she is actively exploring all legal options to intervene. She openly discussed the possibility of stripping ON! of its broadcasting license but warned that doing so requires strict, legally airtight criteria.
Letschert emphasized that she cannot simply ban the broadcaster by decree, as a judge would immediately overturn an arbitrary decision. ON! must be proven to have systematically violated the Media Act and journalistic standards.
ON! was also in hot water a few months earlier. In June, ten fellow public broadcasters sent a joint letter to Letschert refusing to cooperate with ON! due to repeated violations of the journalistic code of conduct.
While the overarching NPO organization acknowledged that ON! regularly breaks the Code of Journalistic Conduct, the NPO stated it lacks the legal mandate to issue sanctions or formally request the minister to expel them. This kicked the responsibility back to Letschert and parliament.

deduped_items.title: Dutch spy agencies to get more powers against foreign enemies
deduped_items.summary: The Netherlands’ two intelligence agencies are to gain new powers to track and disrupt “obvious adversaries” such as Russian hackers,...
deduped_items.body_text:
Dutch spy agencies to get more powers against foreign enemies
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The Netherlands’ two intelligence agencies are to gain new powers to track and disrupt “obvious adversaries” such as Russian hackers, Chinese spies and Iranian operatives without asking permission in advance, under a draft law published by the cabinet.
The domestic intelligence service AIVD and military intelligence service MIVD would no longer need prior sign-off to follow an individual hacker online. “By then they have already gone,” said defence minister Dilan Yesilgöz.
Once a foreign service is formally designated an adversary, the agencies could pursue anyone thought to be working for it, with a watchdog checking afterwards whether their actions were lawful and able to halt operations it considers inappropriate.
The plans have raised concerns about the privacy of Dutch citizens. Yesilgöz said oversight would remain in place. “Putin and his cronies do not deserve our privacy, but the people of the Netherlands do,” she said.
The bill would also let the agencies work more closely with Dutch banks, universities and online platforms, warn them of risks and, in some cases, demand information from them. Interior minister Pieter Heerma, who is responsible for the AIVD, declined to name specific organisations.
It follows the previous cabinet’s abandoned plan to screen 8,000 foreign researchers and students for espionage risks, which was judged unworkable. Oversight of the two agencies would be merged into a single body.
The draft is open for public consultation before it goes to parliament.

deduped_items.summary: Ukraine is about to try Davor Savicic in absentia - the first Bosnian national to be charged with war crimes allegedly committed while fighting with Russian forces in 2022. In an interview with BIRN, one of his accusers recalls his captivity in a rat-infested pit, blindfolded and bound, fearing for his life.

deduped_items.title: EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination
deduped_items.summary: The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely. François Wakenhut was responding to an open […] The post EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination appeared first o
deduped_items.body_text:
Temporary chemical measures on affected roads must not distract from the fact that the government still lacks a genuine and transparent action plan.Continue reading
The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely.
François Wakenhut was responding to an open letter written in early July by 14 international anti-asbestos occupational safety, health, and environmental protection organizations and experts to the leaders of the European Union and Hungary.
In the document, they drew attention to the gravity of the situation in Szombathely, highlighting the dangers posed by the contamination, posing a particular threat to children’s health.
In a letter written on behalf of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the director-general emphasized that it is primarily the responsibility of the competent national authorities to ensure compliance with applicable EU rules in such cases, to assess the risks, and to take the necessary protective and remediation measures.
The European Commission is confident that the national authorities will continue to act swiftly and decisively to protect public health in the affected areas,”
François Wakenhut stated.
The asbestos contamination scandal broke out the day after Hungary’s parliamentary elections, when in Vas County the head of the environmental protection department at the local government office and the mayor of Szombathely announced at an emergency press conference that, in one of the city’s single-family residential areas, on several streets of the “Oladi Plateau,” crushed stone containing asbestos had been spread years earlier. Airborne asbestos fibers are seriously harmful to health.
István Orbán, director general of the government office, said that, according to reports, four quarries in Burgenland, Austria, had previously been closed due to high asbestos content, and they suspect the material may have come from there.
András Nemény, mayor of Szombathely, announced that 12 kilometers of streets in that part of the city are covered with asbestos-contaminated crushed stone, and the cost of safely removing and disposing of it exceeds the city’s financial resources.
To access the force majeure fund, he appealed to both the outgoing government and the incoming government for assistance. Tibor Navracsics, the outgoing Minister of Regional Development, promised to make the fund available, and a supporting government resolution was passed, but only the local government was able to take concrete steps; to prevent dust from spreading, they began regularly watering the affected streets and even applied a layer of bitumen to some sections, while awaiting guidance from experts on exactly what steps to take.
In the following weeks, several municipalities in Vas County—including Kőszeg, Lukácsháza, Bük, and Sárvár—reported that they might also be affected; laboratory tests revealed asbestos levels exceeding the threshold in all of these locations.
In Táplánszentkereszt, the areas in front of the daycare center, kindergarten, and school were inadvertently covered with asbestos-containing material; there, too, the local government had no other option but to spray the area with calcium chloride. In Bük, the local government had the material removed at its own expense, in compliance with regulations governing hazardous materials.
In Szombathely, weekly public forums were held; construction in the area was halted due to the imposed restrictions, and heavy vehicle traffic was temporarily banned and then restricted during certain periods.
On May 21, the Hungarian prime minister held talks in Vienna with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker.
They announced that a joint Hungarian

deduped_items.body_text:
Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
Prague Morning
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.
Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.
At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.
The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.
The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.
The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.
How the Champions League league phase works
The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.
Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.
The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.
The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

deduped_items.body_text:
MINT Market Returns to Prague's Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
Prague Morning
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.
From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.
The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.
MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.
Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.
For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.
View this post on Instagram
“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.
“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”
The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

deduped_items.body_text:
Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
Prague Morning
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.
The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.
The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.
One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.
Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public
Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.
An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.
Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.
A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.
The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.
A Baroque complex with a long military history
Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.
The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.
Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

deduped_items.title: TAUD Beberkan 6 Temuan Represif Aparat saat Demo 27 Agustus: Ada Penangkapan Sewenang-wenang
deduped_items.summary: TAUD melontarkan kritik pedas terhadap penggunaan istilah “preventive strike” oleh Polda Metro Jaya dalam merespons aksi demonstrasi 27 Agustus 2026
deduped_items.body_text:
Demo di Jakarta
TAUD Beberkan 6 Temuan Represif Aparat saat Demo 27 Agustus: Ada Penangkapan Sewenang-wenang
TAUD melontarkan kritik pedas terhadap penggunaan istilah “preventive strike” oleh Polda Metro Jaya dalam merespons aksi demonstrasi 27 Agustus 2026
Ringkasan Berita:
- TAUD mengungkap sejumlah dugaan tindakan represif dan pelanggaran prosedur yang dilakukan aparat kepolisian dalam pengamanan demonstrasi pada Kamis, 27 Agustus 2026
- TAUD mengecam keras tindakan tersebut karena dinilai melanggar hukum acara pidana dan hak konstitusional warga negara.
- TAUD melontarkan kritik pedas terhadap penggunaan istilah “preventive strike” oleh Polda Metro Jaya dalam merespons aksi demonstrasi 27 Agustus 2026.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA – Tim Advokasi untuk Demokrasi (TAUD) mengungkap sejumlah dugaan tindakan represif dan pelanggaran prosedur yang dilakukan aparat kepolisian dalam pengamanan demonstrasi pada Kamis, 27 Agustus 2026.
Peringatan satu tahun Aksi Agustus 2025 tersebut diwarnai oleh aksi penangkapan sewenang-wenang terhadap massa aksi maupun masyarakat sipil.
Baca juga: Ayahnya Meninggal dalam Kericuhan Demo 27 Agustus, Yoga Kenang Nasihat yang Selalu Diingat
TAUD mengecam keras tindakan tersebut karena dinilai melanggar hukum acara pidana dan hak konstitusional warga negara.
“Upaya paksa sewenang-wenang dengan dalih ‘mengamankan’ oleh Polda Metro Jaya melanggar hukum acara pidana. Hal ini terbukti melalui penangkapan, penyitaan hingga penggeledahan oleh Kepolisian tanpa dasar,” tulis TAUD dalam siaran persnya, Jumat (28/8/2026).
Baca juga: Polisi Amankan 5 Anak Pembawa Buah Bintaro Dicampur Bensin Saat Kerusuhan Usai Demo di DPR
Berdasarkan pemantauan di lapangan dan aduan di hotline, TAUD menghimpun enam temuan utama terkait praktik represif aparat:
1. Penargetan Admin Media Sosial: Aparat Kepolisian diduga melakukan pemantauan dan penargetan terhadap admin media sosial, individu kritis, hingga pihak yang terlibat dalam acara amal untuk korban gempa NTT.
2. Penangkapan Tanpa Prosedur: Sejumlah individu diduga ditangkap tanpa prosedur, dasar hukum, dan bukti yang memadai.
3. Penyisiran di Stasiun: Warga diduga dicegat di beberapa titik stasiun dan digeledah tanpa dasar hukum jelas, lalu beberapa di antaranya dibawa ke Polda Metro Jaya.
4. Pemeriksaan di Jam Tidak Wajar: Terdapat pemeriksaan saksi yang dilakukan pada dini hari tanpa didampingi advokat atau bantuan hukum.
5. Aparat Tanpa Seragam: Ditemukan sejumlah aparat yang dikerahkan di sekitar titik aksi tanpa menggunakan seragam maupun atribut resmi Kepolisian.
6. Penahanan Melebihi 24 Jam: Hingga siaran pers diterbitkan, sejumlah korban penangkapan belum dilepaskan, bahkan beberapa di antaranya telah ditahan lebih dari 24 jam.
TAUD menilai, status “pengamanan” atau pemeriksaan sebagai “saksi” yang digunakan polisi seringkali hanya dalih untuk melakukan perampasan kemerdekaan.
“Status Saksi tidak menghapus kewajiban aparat untuk menempuh prosedur yang sah,” tegas TAUD.
Pihaknya menemukan banyak warga yang ditangkap dengan status saksi, namun tidak dipanggil secara patut dan diperlakukan tidak sesuai dengan asas praduga tidak bersalah.
Selain itu, organisasi yang terdiri antara lain dari YLBHI, KontraS, serta Amnesty International ini menyoroti adanya pemeriksaan terhadap warga di ruang publik atau sweeping hanya berdasarkan atribut atau dugaan akan mengikuti aksi.

deduped_items.body_text:
Alex Eala, Iva Jovic share court with dads in US Open exhibition

Towards the end of the match, the two rising stars brought their fathers onto the court for a brief mixed doubles match, ending the exhibition with a heartwarming moment and a hug with their dads.

deduped_items.body_text:
Nepal floods: Survivors, swallowed by silt, recount horror
BIDUR, Nepal —Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of helicopters echoed across the devastated town of Bidur.
A few walked alone, their faces frozen in shock, as helicopters landed every few minutes on a football field inside the town’s military cantonment, whipping up clouds of dust.
Among the survivors was customs agent Omkar Joshi, who spent the previous night stranded on a hilltop in the border town of Timure before being rescued.
READ: Nepal-Tibet floods: Death toll nears 400, rescuers search for 1,400 missing
“Everything is finished,” Joshi, 35, told AFP, his voice breaking with emotion.
The town he fled had all but vanished beneath a torrent of water, mud and debris.
“Ninety percent” of its people were dead, he said, swallowed by silt.
“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”
He said hundreds of people survived only by scrambling up nearby slopes as floodwaters roared through the valley below.
READ: Breakdown of nationalities missing after Nepal-Tibet flash floods
“It rained all night, but we stayed put till the choppers came for us,” he added.
On Wednesday, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through villages and towns along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Nepali police have recovered 270 bodies, but search operations continue.
Many of the missing are foreign tourists caught in the disaster, which according to the US Geological Survey was caused by a glacial collapse that resulted in an overwhelming flow of icy debris.
Buried alive
In Bidur, scores of anxious relatives peered through the barbed wire separating the football ground from the road, hoping to see the familiar face of a loved one.
Sita BK was searching for her younger brother Ramchandra, a schoolteacher in Timure.
“I spoke to him in the morning just before I heard the news,” said the 37-year-old. “But ever since, his phone is switched off.”
She said she had no choice but to wait.
READ: 1 Filipino missing due to massive Nepal flash flood – tourism board
“They (officials) said their first priority is to rescue people who are contactable,” she said. “But my brother is not.”
Nearby, Anisha Nepali sat quietly in a corner, tears running down her cheeks.
The 24-year-old had rushed back from Kathmandu on Wednesday after hearing about the disaster, but has received no news of her missing mother and younger brother.
“I have given their names, but am yet to hear anything,” she said.
Two young girls climbed out of a helicopter, still in their bright green school uniforms. A rescuer gently caressed their heads and offered them biscuits and water, before leading them away to safety.
Farther downstream, the devastation was etched into the shattered landscape of Devighat.
Residents said only one of roughly 150 houses along the banks of the Trishuli River remained intact: a four-storey old-age care home.
But rescuers said up to seven elderly residents were buried when a landslide crashed into the home as they tried to flee.
Images shared by a rescuer showed one of the victims trapped beneath an uprooted tree.
Sabir Miyan, a resident of the town, said warnings that floodwaters were racing down from the mountains had helped save lives.
“Many of us could save our lives but everything else is gone,” he said. “It is all ruins now.”

deduped_items.body_text:
WASHINGTON: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters “rightfully allocated to it” under the Indus Waters Treaty would have “profound consequences for regional peace and security”.
The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation.
In his virtual address to a Washington seminar on “The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads”, he declared that Pakistan would strongly safeguard its “legitimate rights and interests” under the treaty and international law.
FM Dar said the 1960 agreement remained “valid, binding and fully operative” despite India’s unilateral decision in April 2025 to place it “in abeyance”.
“The treaty contains no provision permitting either party to unilaterally suspend or place it in abeyance,” he said, adding that neither country could, “through a unilateral political declaration, extinguish obligations solemnly undertaken under international law.”
FM Dar said the issue went beyond the bilateral relationship, arguing that it concerned “the sanctity of treaties” and “confidence in international law”.
“If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined,” he said.
He also stressed that geography made cooperation unavoidable, noting that “states cannot alter the direction in which rivers flow”.
“That is precisely why rules matter,” FM Dar said, urging the international community to preserve treaty-based water governance in South Asia.
The foreign minister further said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries had understood that water on which “hundreds of millions of lives depend” was too fundamental to be subjected to fluctuations in political relations.
“Today, however, that principle faces its gravest challenge,” he said.
FM Dar said Pakistan’s position was clear and consistent and that treaty-based proceedings had continued despite India’s assertion of “abeyance”, reinforcing the principle that “unilateral action cannot displace an agreed legal framework”.
Pakistan has pursued arbitration over disputes concerning Indian hydroelectric projects on the Western Rivers, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle.
The Court of Arbitration at The Hague has continued proceedings, with earlier rulings addressing its jurisdiction and questions concerning the interpretation and application of the treaty.
The treaty allocates the three eastern rivers to India and the three western rivers, including the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, primarily to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses.
FM Dar said resorting to the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or a Court of Arbitration “is not an act of confrontation” but “the implementation of the very legal framework to which both countries agreed and are bound”.
“Pakistan has consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and the mechanisms provided under the Treaty,” he said.
He said the dispute was especially serious because Pakistan’s agriculture, food security, energy production, livelihoods and economic development depended heavily on the Indus River system.
“The Indus Basin is the lifeline of more than 250 million Pakistanis,” Dar said. “Water security for Pakistan is therefore inseparable from economic security, food security and, ultimately, national security.”

deduped_items.body_text:
WASHINGTON: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Friday warned that any attempt to deprive Pakistan of waters “rightfully allocated to it” under the Indus Waters Treaty would have “profound consequences for regional peace and security”.
The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation.
In his virtual address to a Washington seminar on “The Indus Waters Treaty: South Asian Security at the Crossroads”, he declared that Pakistan would strongly safeguard its “legitimate rights and interests” under the treaty and international law.
FM Dar said the 1960 agreement remained “valid, binding and fully operative” despite India’s unilateral decision in April 2025 to place it “in abeyance”.
“The treaty contains no provision permitting either party to unilaterally suspend or place it in abeyance,” he said, adding that neither country could, “through a unilateral political declaration, extinguish obligations solemnly undertaken under international law.”
FM Dar said the issue went beyond the bilateral relationship, arguing that it concerned “the sanctity of treaties” and “confidence in international law”.
“If solemn treaty obligations can simply be set aside whenever political relations deteriorate, the very purpose of concluding the treaties is undermined,” he said.
He also stressed that geography made cooperation unavoidable, noting that “states cannot alter the direction in which rivers flow”.
“That is precisely why rules matter,” FM Dar said, urging the international community to preserve treaty-based water governance in South Asia.
The foreign minister further said the treaty had survived wars, military crises, diplomatic breakdowns and prolonged political tensions for more than six decades because both countries had understood that water on which “hundreds of millions of lives depend” was too fundamental to be subjected to fluctuations in political relations.
“Today, however, that principle faces its gravest challenge,” he said.
FM Dar said Pakistan’s position was clear and consistent and that treaty-based proceedings had continued despite India’s assertion of “abeyance”, reinforcing the principle that “unilateral action cannot displace an agreed legal framework”.
Pakistan has pursued arbitration over disputes concerning Indian hydroelectric projects on the Western Rivers, particularly Kishenganga and Ratle.
The Court of Arbitration at The Hague has continued proceedings, with earlier rulings addressing its jurisdiction and questions concerning the interpretation and application of the treaty.
The treaty allocates the three eastern rivers to India and the three western rivers, including the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, primarily to Pakistan, subject to specified Indian uses.
FM Dar said resorting to the Permanent Indus Commission, a neutral expert or a Court of Arbitration “is not an act of confrontation” but “the implementation of the very legal framework to which both countries agreed and are bound”.
“Pakistan has consistently sought to resolve differences through dialogue, diplomacy and the mechanisms provided under the Treaty,” he said.
He said the dispute was especially serious because Pakistan’s agriculture, food security, energy production, livelihoods and economic development depended heavily on the Indus River system.
“The Indus Basin is the lifeline of more than 250 million Pakistanis,” Dar said. “Water security for Pakistan is therefore inseparable from economic security, food security and, ultimately, national security.”
Against this backdrop, he warned that unilateral interference with the treaty could affect not only South Asian stability but also create “a dangerous precedent for treaty

  - By Crystal Hsu / Staff reporter
 Taiwan’s population is projected to shrink by almost half over the next five decades, intensifying labor shortages and placing a growing drag on economic growth as the technology-intensive economy confronts a rapidly aging workforce. The population is expected to fall to 12.15 million by 2075, a 48 percent decline from this year, National Development Council projections released yesterday showed. The decline would fundamentally alter Taiwan’s workforce. From 2037, more than half of the working-age population is projected to be aged between 45 and 64, signaling the end of an era when the economy could rely on a relatively large labor force. Children climb on playground equipment at a park in Taipei yesterday.Photo: CNA The shift threatens to challenge Taiwan’s growth model, which depends on a broad manufacturing workforce and a growing supply of highly skilled workers to support its semiconductor and artificial intelligence industries. A shrinking pool of workers could make recruitment increasingly difficult, while a growing elderly population would add pressure on social spending and public finances. The projections also point to a deeper demographic problem — Taiwan is not only losing its population, but failing to replenish it, the council said. It lowered its long-term fertility assumptions after the fertility rate fell to a record low 0.695 last year, significantly below previous estimates. The number of women aged 20 to 49 has declined since peaking in 2005, while the proportion of married women in that age group has also fallen. The shrinking pool of potential mothers is making a sustained recovery in births increasingly difficult, it said. Taiwan’s population is projected to fall below 20 million in 2045, dropping to 19.98 million. People aged 65 or older are expected to account for 37 percent of the population, while the working-age population would shrink to 57.9 percent and children to just 5.2 percent, the council said. By 2075, the imbalance would be even more pronounced, with older people projected to comprise 52.9 percent of the population, working-age people 42.3 percent and children 4.8 percent, it said. The dependency ratio — the number of children and elderly people relative to those of working age — is projected to rise from 55.2 dependents for every 100 working-age people to 136.6 by 2075, the council said. The potential support ratio is expected to fall below one, suggesting less than one working-age person for every person aged 65 or older, it said. The government is preparing the economy for a permanently smaller workforce. It has established a population strategy task force, and in May launched 18 measures covering childbirth support, childcare, education, workplace policies and housing. Additional policy packages would target elderly people, talent development across all age groups and the recruitment of overseas talent, the council said. For businesses, the implications extend beyond hiring. Companies are likely to face greater pressure to raise labor force participation among elderly people, attract workers from overseas, and accelerate automation and productivity gains.

deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            CEC approves nuclear referendum, rejects other twoCONDEMNED: The KMT slammed the rejections, saying the CEC decided on behalf of 23 million people, while the TPP said it brought shame to Taiwan’s democratic system
  - By Hsu Yung-ching / Staff reporter
 The Central Election Commission (CEC) yesterday announced it has approved holding a referendum on nuclear power, but rejected proposals on caning and traffic fines. The Legislative Yuan on Aug. 14 approved three referendums: introducing caning as a criminal punishment, abolishing the government’s nuclear-free homeland policy and using traffic fines to improve road safety. The commission met for more than two and a half hours, and ruled that the referendum on caning did not meet the requirements of the Referendum Act (公民投票法), CEC Chairman Michael You (游盈隆) said. Central Election Commission Chairman Michael You speaks at a news conference in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Chen Yi-kuan, Taipei Times The caning proposal, put forward by the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT), seeks to introduce caning as a punishment for sexual assault, crimes against children, large-scale fraud and aggravated fraud. However, caning or similar forms of corporal punishment are not recognized under Taiwan’s criminal justice system, You said. The CEC therefore determined that the proposal amounted to creating new legislative principles, and was not a referendum on the initiation or repeal of a major policy, as defined by the act, he added. The proposal involves using state power to inflict physical pain on prisoners and is considered by many countries to be cruel, inhuman and a violation of human dignity, he said. That would contravene the Act Governing Execution of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (公民與政治權利國際公約及經濟社會文化權利國際公約施行法), which states that no one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, he added. Of the eight CEC members, seven voted that the caning proposal did not qualify as a referendum, said You, who chaired the meeting, adding that he did not cast a vote. Regarding the Taiwan People’s Party’s (TPP) proposed referendum on earmarking traffic fines exclusively for road-related purposes, four commission members found that it did not meet the requirements of the Referendum Act, he said. The commission held three rounds of voting, with the same 4-3 split each time, he added. As for the proposal to repeal Taiwan’s nuclear-free homeland policy, six CEC members supported the referendum, with one abstention, You said. The CEC ruled that the proposal meets the requirements of the Referendum Act, he said, adding that the referendum vote would be held on Nov. 28, alongside the local elections. The KMT caucus condemned the CEC’s decision to reject the two proposals, saying that referendums exist to give people a direct say when a country faces major disputes over public policy. “Yet what has happened now is that whether people want to vote no longer matters, and neither does whether the Legislative Yuan approves the proposal,” it said. “Instead the CEC has decided on behalf of 23 million people: ‘You are not entitled to answer this question.’” “Is this direct democracy, or the direct confiscation of democracy?” it asked. The TPP slammed You, saying he had claimed that “referendums submitted by the Legislative Yuan should be approved in principle and rejected only as an exception.” “Yet he has now turned that exception into a pretext for arbitrarily expanding his powers, abandoning his principles as an academic, enabling the ruling party to flout the law and obstructing the public’s right to initiate referendums,” it said. “Such actions have brought shame on Taiwan’s democratic constitutional system.” Additional reporting by Lin Hsin-han

deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Prosecutors indict nine in Dr Shine hidden camera case
  - By Wang Ting-chuan and Jake Chung / Staff reporter, with staff writer
 Prosecutors yesterday indicted nine people for allegedly installing hidden surveillance cameras in eight Dr Shine (光澤) clinics in Taipei and New Taipei City, and secretly recording more than 300 patients — including four minors — while they were exposed. Investigations into other branches allegedly involved in the case are still ongoing. The New Taipei City District Prosecutors’ Office is seeking a prison term of 16 years for Dr Shine group operations manager Chen Chih-min (陳志敏), 14 years for company information department head Tang Yung-chieh (唐詠傑) and seven years for surveillance camera supplier Chang Chao-ming (張朝銘). A branch of the Dr Shine cosmetics chain is pictured in New Taipei City in an undated photograph.Photo: Hsu Sheng-lun, Taipei Times They also proposed seven years for Dr Shine employee Chiang Chin-wei (江勁緯) and unspecified prison terms for five other employees embroiled in the case. Chen and Tang had abused clients’ trust, shown no remorse, offered no public apology and attempted to deceive police into believing that the devices had been removed years earlier, so they should receive severe sentences, the prosecutors’ office said in the indictment. Prosecutors also called on Dr Shine owner Wang Chao-huei (王朝輝) to return to Taiwan to face investigation over the scandal. Wang traveled to China before the incident came to light, but has allegedly shown no sign of willingly returning to Taiwan, even after a wanted notice was issued for him. Chen and Tang allegedly installed surveillance cameras disguised as smoke detectors or sensor-activated lighting at two Dr Shine clinics in New Taipei City’s Banciao District (板橋); and one each in Sanxia District (三峽), Sanchong District (三重) and Sinjhuang District (新莊), prosecutors said. They installed the same devices at clinics in Taipei’s Guting District (古亭), Daan District (大安) and Songshan District (松山), they added. Tang allegedly created a Line group that included Chen and others, and used it to direct efforts to remove surveillance cameras from all branches between May 5 and May 8, prosecutors said. The installation of cameras allegedly gave Chen and Tang access to private moments when patients were exposed, severely infringing on people’s constitutionally guaranteed rights to privacy and self-determination, prosecutors added.

deduped_items.title: 《TAIPEI TIMES》 Population to plummet, council warns
deduped_items.summary: INCREASING IMBALANCE:The percentage of working-age people is expected to shrink to 42.3% of the popu...…
deduped_items.body_text:
《TAIPEI TIMES》 Population to plummet, council warns
Children climb on playground equipment at a park in Taipei yesterday. Photo: CNA
INCREASING IMBALANCE:The percentage of working-age people is expected to shrink to 42.3% of the population, while older people would comprise 52.9%, the agency said
By Crystal Hsu / Staff reporter
Taiwan’s population is projected to shrink by almost half over the next five decades, intensifying labor shortages and placing a growing drag on economic growth as the technology-intensive economy confronts a rapidly aging workforce.
The population is expected to fall to 12.15 million by 2075, a 48 percent decline from this year, National Development Council projections released yesterday showed.
The decline would fundamentally alter Taiwan’s workforce. From 2037, more than half of the working-age population is projected to be aged between 45 and 64, signaling the end of an era when the economy could rely on a relatively large labor force.
The shift threatens to challenge Taiwan’s growth model, which depends on a broad manufacturing workforce and a growing supply of highly skilled workers to support its semiconductor and artificial intelligence industries.
A shrinking pool of workers could make recruitment increasingly difficult, while a growing elderly population would add pressure on social spending and public finances.
The projections also point to a deeper demographic problem — Taiwan is not only losing its population, but failing to replenish it, the council said.
It lowered its long-term fertility assumptions after the fertility rate fell to a record low 0.695 last year, significantly below previous estimates.
The number of women aged 20 to 49 has declined since peaking in 2005, while the proportion of married women in that age group has also fallen.
The shrinking pool of potential mothers is making a sustained recovery in births increasingly difficult, it said.
Taiwan’s population is projected to fall below 20 million in 2045, dropping to 19.98 million.
People aged 65 or older are expected to account for 37 percent of the population, while the working-age population would shrink to 57.9 percent and children to just 5.2 percent, the council said.
By 2075, the imbalance would be even more pronounced, with older people projected to comprise 52.9 percent of the population, working-age people 42.3 percent and children 4.8 percent, it said.
The dependency ratio — the number of children and elderly people relative to those of working age — is projected to rise from 55.2 dependents for every 100 working-age people to 136.6 by 2075, the council said.
The potential support ratio is expected to fall below one, suggesting less than one working-age person for every person aged 65 or older, it said.
The government is preparing the economy for a permanently smaller workforce. It has established a population strategy task force, and in May launched 18 measures covering childbirth support, childcare, education, workplace policies and housing.
Additional policy packages would target elderly people, talent development across all age groups and the recruitment of overseas talent, the council said.
For businesses, the implications extend beyond hiring. Companies are likely to face greater pressure to raise labor force participation among elderly people, attract workers from overseas, and accelerate automation and productivity gains.

INCREASING IMBALANCE:The percentage of working-age people is expected to shrink to 42.3% of the population, while older people would comprise 52.9%, the agency said
By Crystal Hsu / Staff reporter
Taiwan’s population is projected to shrink by almost half over the next five decades, intensifying labor shortages and placing a growing drag on economic growth as the technology-intensive economy confronts a rapidly aging workforce.
The population is expected to fall to 12.15 million by 2075, a 48 percent decline from this year, National Development Council projections released yesterday showed.
The decline would fundamentally alter Taiwan’s workforce. From 2037, more than half of the working-age population is projected to be aged between 45 and 64, signaling the end of an era when the economy could rely on a relatively large labor force.
The shift threatens to challenge Taiwan’s growth model, which depends on a broad manufacturing workforce and a growing supply of highly skilled workers to support its semiconductor and artificial intelligence industries.
A shrinking pool of workers could make recruitment increasingly difficult, while a growing elderly population would add pressure on social spending and public finances.
The projections also point to a deeper demographic problem — Taiwan is not only losing its population, but failing to replenish it, the council said.
It lowered its long-term fertility assumptions after the fertility rate fell to a record low 0.695 last year, significantly below previous estimates.
The number of women aged 20 to 49 has declined since peaking in 2005, while the proportion of married women in that age group has also fallen.
The shrinking pool of potential mothers is making a sustained recovery in births increasingly difficult, it said.
Taiwan’s population is projected to fall below 20 million in 2045, dropping to 19.98 million.
People aged 65 or older are expected to account for 37 percent of the population, while the working-age population would shrink to 57.9 percent and children to just 5.2 percent, the council said.
By 2075, the imbalance would be even more pronounced, with older people projected to comprise 52.9 percent of the population, working-age people 42.3 percent and children 4.8 percent, it said.
The dependency ratio — the number of children and elderly people relative to those of working age — is projected to rise from 55.2 dependents for every 100 working-age people to 136.6 by 2075, the council said.
The potential support ratio is expected to fall below one, suggesting less than one working-age person for every person aged 65 or older, it said.
The government is preparing the economy for a permanently smaller workforce. It has established a population strategy task force, and in May launched 18 measures covering childbirth support, childcare, education, workplace policies and housing.
Additional policy packages would target elderly people, talent development across all age groups and the recruitment of overseas talent, the council said.
For businesses, the implications extend beyond hiring. Companies are likely to face greater pressure to raise labor force participation among elderly people, attract workers from overseas, and accelerate automation and productivity gains.
